edits.hypothesis: Automatically appending a newline to keystrokes that lack one prevents the common failure mode where commands hang or concatenate when the policy forgets the trailing newline.
edits.why_not_lower_lever: A prompt instruction is often ignored by the policy under pressure; auto-correcting in the parser mechanism is robust and reliable.
edits.trigger_condition: when parsed keystrokes do not end with a newline character
edits.retroactive_check: corrective: bn-fit-modify would have avoided hanging/concatenation issues; preservative: standard commands already ending in newline are untouched; transfer: applies universally to any task where commands are sent without newlines.
edits.regression_risk: extremely low, as command lines in a shell always require a trailing newline to execute.
edits.mechanism: Automatically appending a newline to keystrokes that lack one prevents the common failure mode where commands hang or concatenate when the policy forgets the trailing newline.

mechanism: Automatically append newline to command keystrokes if missing to prevent command concatenation/hanging failures.
